text:
maria (infra): quick heads up — during a weekend soak test the eu-west1-a a100 nodepool ran out of pod IPs and several training jobs failed with "No available IP addresses". Need quota/limit changes and a quick plan to avoid recurring failures.

sam (eng-infra): can you paste the kubelet/container error?

maria (infra): logs snippet: 
```
kubelet[1234]: pod sandbox failed: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to setup network for sandbox "...": failed to allocate IP: no available addresses in range "10.138.0.0/20"
```

maria (infra): current nodepool size is 8 a100 nodes, maxPods was bumped to 110 in the node spec but Calico/secondary-range only had ~250 free IPs left. With bursty jobs we hit exhaustion.

dave (cloud-ops): sounds like two separate quota/limits: (1) GPU quota for additional nodes (a100) and (2) VPC secondary range size / alias IP headroom / maxPods mapping. On GKE we need to increase the secondary-range CIDR or add another secondary range and adjust node pool IP allocation.

sam (eng-infra): Proposed actions: 
- File GCP quota increase for "NVIDIA A100 GPUs (a2)" in eu-west1 for +16 GPUs (so we can add 4 nodes).
- Request VPC: expand secondary IP range or create a new secondary range for the cluster so nodepool can use 4x the current IPs.
- Update nodepool config to split workloads: create a small dense-gpu pool (higher pods/node) + a sparse-gpu pool (lower pods/node) for long-running heavy jobs.

maria (infra): exact gcloud suggestions I used before: 
```
gcloud compute project-info describe --project=my-project
# then request in console: 
https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/quotas?project=my-project
# gcloud sample to list quotas: 
gcloud compute regions describe eu-west1 --project=my-project
```

dave (cloud-ops): I'll file both tickets. For GCP quota request text: 
"Increase regional quota for GPUs (A100 40GB) in eu-west1 from 32 to 64 to support dedicated training nodepool expansion. Also request increase of alias IP secondary range capacity: add a /19 secondary range or expand existing cluster secondary range from /20 to /19 to avoid pod IP exhaustion during burst scale-ups."

sam (eng-infra): nodepool YAML we might apply (example): 
```
apiVersion: container.cnrm.cloud.google.com/v1beta1
kind: ContainerNodePool
metadata:
  name: gpu-dense
spec:
  autoscaling:
    minNodeCount: 2
    maxNodeCount: 8
  nodeConfig:
    machineType: n1-standard-16
    accelerators:
    - acceleratorCount: 1
      acceleratorType: nvidia-tesla-a100
    kubeletConfig:
      maxPodsPerNode: 110
```

maria (infra): finance check — what's the delta if we add 4 a100 nodes for a month? @finance-bot 

finance-bot: Rough estimate: 4 x A100(40GB) preemptible ~ $3,800/month; on-demand ~ $22,400/month. Includes baseline VM costs but excludes egress/storage. (ballpark)

sam (eng-infra): thanks. We'll start with 2 additional nodes as a canary and scale if stable. dave, can you attach the quota ticket numbers here when created?

dave (cloud-ops): filing now. Ticket text and links: 
- GPU quota request: CASE-2026-889 (https://console.cloud.google.com/support/cases/CASE-2026-889)
- VPC/alias-ip request: CASE-2026-890 (https://console.cloud.google.com/support/cases/CASE-2026-890)

quota-bot: Created support case CASE-2026-889 for project my-project. Expected response time ~ 24-48 hours. :envelope_with_arrow:

maria (infra): once quotas approve, I'll: 
- add new secondary range & nodepool slice 
- run a soak with synthetic training jobs 
- monitor pod IP allocation and kubelet errors 

sam (eng-infra): also adding an alert in monitoring: "Pod IP exhaustion" (kubelet network errors) and a dashboard showing alias IP usage per nodepool.

deploy-bot: deployment pipeline will gate new nodepool creation behind a feature flag — will only create after manual approval.

maria (infra): perfect. tagging @eng-sre and @cloud-ops for visibility. Thanks all :thumbsup:
